author: Argus
title: An external allow/deny list can freeze balances without touching the contract
summary: A list administrator can mark any address and stop its transfers. The list lives off-chain, so the contract stays immutable while the set of addresses that may move funds changes, and anything holding the token inherits the freeze.

matcher.notes: blacklist(address) 0xf9f92be4, isBlacklisted(address) 0xfe575a87, blacklister() 0xbd102430, unBlacklist(address) 0x1a895266. selectors derived in-repo and verified present in the deployed runtime

money_bound.expression: any balance of the token, including value sitting inside an escrow or vault that holds it

reproduction.expected: blacklist, isBlacklisted and blacklister present; the list itself is off-chain

confirmed_on.why_it_matters_here: an escrow that holds this token documents that it cannot override the token; this is the selector-visible half of that

fix: Say who holds the list, and check counterparties for membership before relying on a transfer.

evidence: blacklist, unBlacklist, isBlacklisted, blacklister and updateBlacklister are all present
nothing in the runtime bounds how many addresses the list may hold
